rv.q: All in all, "Engines and Instruments of Flight" is a most wonderful Jackalope achievement and, should you be a theater worker or a writer or a Kushner superfan or a student of American drama, I think you will be blown away.
For a play that’s inspired so completely by a previous one, this is a surprisingly inspired and even epic work.
It’s a loving and enjoyable tribute to Tony Kushner and Angels In America.
The depths of its script are right up there with James Lapine and Stephen Sondheim’s Sunday in the Park with George or Jonthan Larson’s Tick Tick Boom .
ENGINES AND INSTRUMENTS OF FLIGHT: A Fantasia in Three Acts is a unique theatrical spectacle.
The result is thoughtful, moving, provocative, and deeply ambitious.
It is unusual, imaginative, ambitious, and unlike anything you are likely to find in the traditional holiday theatre lineup.

cn.t: Critics largely praise this ambitious "Angels in America" deconstruction as a fascinating, niche theatrical achievement, with standout direction and scope.
